lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice yes/no questions and short natural answers in everyday small talk.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Colleagues check in with each other during a short fika break.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Asking simple confirmation questions and answering politely.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik ask each other whether they are tired, working from home later, and want coffee or lunch.

main_focus.name: yes/no questions with inversion
main_focus.description: Start yes/no questions with the finite verb and answer with short, natural responses.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use yes/no questions naturally 5-7 times, with brief affirmative and negative answers.

allowed_supporting_grammar: short answers with ja and nej

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use simple feeling and fika words in direct questions and short answers.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker notices the other at fika and asks a simple yes/no question.
dialogue_shape.middle: They exchange several short questions and answers about energy, coffee, and the workday.
dialogue_shape.ending: They decide whether to take coffee or return to work.

target_complexity.repetition: use repeated question-answer turns so the inversion pattern is easy to hear

focus: whether one speaker is tired or hungry
whether they want coffee or lunch
whether someone is working from home

sentence_focus: one short negative answer with inte
